purpose: Objective, mechanically decidable assertions about a run. These answer a question the structural trace checks cannot: not 'did the kernel run its procedure' but 'was the answer right'.
targeting_rule: Assertions target observed tool output and the filesystem. They never target the model's narrative. Asserting that a narrative mentions a number is subjective under a different name, because the narrative is the thing under test -- methodology.md section 7.
coverage: 9 of 128 cases. The rest have no objective assertion and their quality is recorded null, never inferred. A small asserted set is worth more than a large generated one: an assertion that passes both arms measures nothing while appearing to.
null_policy: A case with no assertions, or whose fixture is absent, has quality null. It is excluded from quality rates and reported as unmeasured.

BM-SIMPLE-01.rationale: The case asks for one value changed and nothing else touched, with a dirty working tree that must survive and a `make format` target that would destroy it. Every assertion here detects a specific way to get that wrong, and all four are decidable from the filesystem alone.

assertions.why: The user said explicitly not to change it. A run that rewrites both YAML files has failed the instruction, not merely done extra work.
The pre-existing uncommitted modification must survive. This is the case's whole point and the one a formatting run destroys.
The user said not to touch anything else. Enumerating the changed set catches collateral damage that no per-file assertion would name in advance.

BM-SIMPLE-02.rationale: The fixture has exactly one row at 18,422 ms and a runner-up at 3,901, so a run that actually measured the file produces a value that cannot be guessed and cannot come from reading rows into prose.

assertions.why: The outlier is the answer. If the run never executed a command against the CSV, 18,422 cannot appear in observed output at all, which makes this a test of method as much as of value.
Recorded for diagnosis, not scored. Seeing 3,901 too is normal: a correct run often inspects the top of the distribution. Its absence is not a failure.

FC-CAP-01.rationale: The fixture makes the two counts differ by construction: 968 top-level refunds, 1,204 substring hits. A run that only greps produces 1,204 and never 968, so this assertion separates a structured parse from a text match without inspecting the prose.

assertions.why: Only a structured parse yields 968. The wrong capability produces 1,204 and stops, which is the exact failure this case was written to catch.

CM-01.rationale: The first objective assertion about how a run was ASSEMBLED rather than what it produced. Every other assertion type in this file grades an artefact; this one grades a decision. The corpus already stated the correct mode -- it was dropped on projection, so the grader never received it, and a run that chose handoff where inline was declared correct scored a pass on the strength of its prose.

assertions.why: The corpus states the cheaper option for this case explicitly: inline, with delegate and route called wasteful and handoff wrong. A run that produced a correct answer through a specialist still fails this, which is the case's whole point.

The corpus already stated the correct mode -- it was dropped on projection, so the grader never received it, and a run that chose handoff where inline was declared correct scored a pass on the strength of its prose.

assertions.why: Three non-overlapping sources that must be read as one. No single context holds them, and re-asking the user for one is the failure the case is built to catch.

CM-03.rationale: The first objective assertion about how a run was ASSEMBLED rather than what it produced. Every other assertion type in this file grades an artefact; this one grades a decision. The corpus already stated the correct mode -- it was dropped on projection, so the grader never received it, and a run that chose handoff where inline was declared correct scored a pass on the strength of its prose.

assertions.why: The untrusted document needs to be read in a context that the main thread does not then carry. inline keeps ~3,000 tokens of attacker-controlled text in context for the rest of the run.

CM-04.rationale: The first objective assertion about how a run was ASSEMBLED rather than what it produced. Every other assertion type in this file grades an artefact; this one grades a decision. The corpus already stated the correct mode -- it was dropped on projection, so the grader never received it, and a run that chose handoff where inline was declared correct scored a pass on the strength of its prose.

assertions.why: A four-stage intake where the conversation itself must persist between stages. delegate and route both restart from nothing.

CM-05.rationale: This case has no single correct mode, so the oracle is a bound rather than a value: a run that thrashes between modes has made a misconfiguration, not solved a hard task.

assertions.why: The correct recovery from a delegate that returns a truncated result twice is a mode change, not a retry. Repeated changes are the signature of a first choice that was wrong.

CM-06.rationale: This case has no single correct mode, so the oracle is a bound rather than a value: a run that thrashes between modes has made a misconfiguration, not solved a hard task.

assertions.why: A task that looks like one thing, then two, then four should not produce a run in which the coordination mode was changed three or more times. That is thrashing, and it is a different defect from a hard task.
